Subject: ArborHealth SIG follow-up: subprocessor residency & evidentiary ask

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of ArborHealth's onboarding we need to finish the SIG/CAIQ mapping and collect a compact set of evidentiary artifacts focused on subprocessors and data residency. Specifically we need: 

- An up-to-date subprocessor roster (name, country of operation, purpose, data types processed, KMS/residency notes). CSV preferred.
- For any subprocessor that performs telemetry/metrics or persistent storage, a short note on telemetry retention and whether telemetry is encrypted at rest.
- A redacted SOC 2 excerpt that demonstrates encryption/key management and vendor management controls (we can accept a redacted PDF).
- A draft SIG matrix or CAIQ mapping for our procurement team to review (spreadsheet is fine).

Target: would you be able to provide the above by end-of-day Friday, Jul 3? If not, please propose a delivery plan with owners. Also confirm any subprocessors that are multi-region vs single-region so we can finish our residency assessment.

We may share this package with ArborHealth's InfoSec and Procurement (cc'ed). If you need an NDA amendment for any artifacts, let me know.

Appreciate it,
Dana Ortiz
Security Program Manager
ArborHealth Systems

--

Adding a few technical clarifications from the runtime side that will help the SIG mapping: 

- Subprocessors of note: EdgeCache Inc. (CDN, multi-region, handles streaming prefix content), QuantifyAI (model quantization/compilation, US-based), Telemetrix (ops telemetry; retention configurable per-customer), KeyVaultCo (KMS/HSM provider - customer-specific keys possible).
- Telemetry: our default telemetry is aggregated and anonymized for runtime metrics; persistent KV/prefix caches are encrypted at rest with keys owned by KeyVaultCo. For customers that request dedicated KMS we can provide attestations of key separation.
- SOC 2 notes: the SOC 2 redaction will remove IPs and raw logs; we'll include control references and the sections on encryption, vendor management, and change control.

I'll prepare a short README to accompany the CSV so ArborHealth can map each row to SIG/CAIQ questions.
